items.title: Russia says its drones struck military cargo ship near Odesa
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces attacked port infrastructure and vessels used by Ukraine's military, claiming a dry-cargo ship carrying military supplies was hit at sea while approaching Odesa. The ministry did not identify the vessel or detail the damage.

items.title: Two former Kursk lawmakers detained over border fortification funds
items.summary: Kursk regional governor Alexander Khinshtein said former regional lawmakers Biryukov and Glushkov were detained in an investigation into construction of fortifications along the Ukrainian border. Investigators suspect involvement in embezzling and cashing out public funds allocated to the defences; no conviction was reported.

items.title: Poland rules out sending troops to Ukraine after ceasefire
items.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Warsaw does not intend to deploy troops to Ukraine after hostilities end under the Coalition of the Willing's plan. He made the remarks while commenting on NATO exercises taking place in Poland.

items.title: Zelensky says Coalition of the Willing supports Ukraine joining NATO
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said members of the Coalition of the Willing had voiced support for Ukraine's accession to NATO. The reported endorsement does not constitute an invitation to join the alliance or a change in its formal membership requirements.

items.title: Russian military-linked analysis reports Ukrainian advances in Dnipropetrovsk gray zone
items.summary: A Russian military-linked battlefield assessment says Ukrainian units are consolidating positions in contested parts of Dnipropetrovsk region and advancing in small groups near Komar, Fedorivka and the Mokri Yaly River. It describes sustained fighting and Russian strikes on those positions, without claiming a decisive territorial breakthrough.
